full_judgment: 9. It is true, in the unreported case i.e. in Trade Mark Application No. 6 of 2001, the Karachi case, namely, the decision reported in PLD 1973 (Karachi) 279, was referred to and relied on by one of the parties but on a perusal of the judgment it does not appear that the said decision was at all considered by the Court in disposing the application because there is no mention as to whether that decision was at all considered by the Court and/or whether that decision had any relevance with the facts and circumstances of that case rather, without adverting to the aforesaid decision the Court disposed of that application on merit. Therefore, from a perusal of that judgment it does not appear to me that the Court considered the Karachi case and disagreed with the principle of law laid down therein. I have studied the Karachi decision as best as I could and it appears that the facts of that case are similar to the facts of the present case. In the Karachi case, one Basra Soap Factory filed on 16-6-1950, application No. 30981 for registration of a Trade Mark for Soap in class-3. While that application was pending before the Registry, the Punjab Soap Factory made an application, No. 37079 for registration of their Trade Mark on 16-6-1962 in respect of Soap in Class-3. The Punjab Soap Factory filed an opposition in the proceeding then pending on Application No. 30981 of Basra Soap Factory. But before this opposition could be decided the Trade Mark Registry registered the Trade Mark of the Punjab Soap Factory. Consequently, when Basra Soap Factory's application for registration of its Trade Mark and the opposition filed therein came up for hearing the Registrar rejected the application of the Basra Soap Factory under section 10 (1) of the Act.
